extracted.intended_audience: auditors and audit managers performing OMB Circular A-133 single audits; audit firms and auditee accounting staff; audit quality reviewers (DoD OIG, cognizant agencies)
extracted.subtask_description: Quality control review criteria and procedural requirements for evaluating an auditor's A-133 single audit work (planning, workpapers, internal control testing, reporting, and coordination with other audit organizations). Targets audit firms, cognizant agencies, and auditees subject to OMB Circular A-133 and GAGAS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Control Review Objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the FY audit report submitted to the Single Audit Clearinghouse met the applicable reporting standards and whether the auditor conducted the audit in accordance with applicable standards and OMB Circular A-133.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review scope includes financial statements, major programs, and whether the reporting package and auditor's conduct complied with Circular A-133, GAGAS, and generally accepted auditing standards (see Appendix A for scope and methodology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications of auditors
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether auditors performing the single audit are qualified to perform the engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the qualitative aspects the quality control review focuses on; evaluate staff competence relative to the audit objectives and programs under review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the auditor's independence in fact and appearance for the single audit engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence is a required qualitative aspect reviewed under the quality control review to ensure objectivity of audit findings and opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due professional care
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether auditors exercised due professional care in planning, supervising, performing, and documenting the audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes appropriate application of auditing standards, professional judgment, and sufficiency of evidence to support conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm-level quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the audit firm's quality control policies and whether they were applied to the single audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the firm's quality control system produced adequate planning, supervision, review, and documentation consistent with guidance and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning and supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditors must plan and supervise the audit effectively, including performing procedures to understand the design of internal controls and whether controls have been implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAGAS and generally accepted auditing standards require specific procedures during planning to understand control design and implementation; planning should assess the five components of internal control as part of audit planning to ensure efficient and adequate audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal control and compliance testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditors must test internal control over compliance and evaluate compliance requirements for major programs in accordance with Circular A-133 and the Compliance Supplement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing must consider each applicable compliance requirement and evaluate the five components of internal control for each; testing should be documented in working papers to support audit conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards (SEFA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards in the reporting package and obtain a related opinion where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEFA and related opinion are required elements of a complete A-133 reporting package submitted to the Single Audit Clearinghouse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of Findings and Questioned Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare and include a Schedule of Findings and Questioned Costs in the reporting package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This schedule is a required component of the reporting package and is reviewed as a qualitative aspect of the single audit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Collection Form (DCF) certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Data Collection Form certified by the auditee that the audit was completed according to OMB Circular A-133.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DCF is a required element of the reporting package; certification by the auditee is necessary for submission to the Single Audit Clearinghouse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete reporting package requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The auditee must submit a complete reporting package to the Single Audit Clearinghouse that includes the DCF, financial statements and opinion, SEFA and opinion, report on internal control and compliance related to financial statements, report on internal control over compliance and compliance with laws/regulations/contracts (including opinion on major programs), and Schedule of Findings and Questioned Costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include any required element may render the reporting package incomplete under Circular A-133.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the OMB Compliance Supplement
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditors should use the annually issued Compliance Supplement to determine audit scope for review of internal control and to identify objectives and characteristics of internal control for each compliance requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Supplement gives examples of common characteristics for the five components of internal control and assists in determining applicable requirements and audit procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify applicable compliance requirements (14 categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditors must identify which of the 14 compliance requirements in the Compliance Supplement apply to the auditee's major programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 14 compliance requirements include Activities Allowed/Unallowed; Allowable Costs/Cost Principles; Cash Management; Eligibility; Equipment and Real Property Management; Matching/Level of Effort/Earmarking; Period of Availability; Procurement and Suspension/Debarment; Davis-Bacon Act; Program Income; Real Property Acquisition/Relocation Assistance; Reporting; Subrecipient Monitoring; Special Tests and Provisions. Mark which apply to the sampled awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of the five components of internal control
rubrics_metrics.description: For each applicable compliance requirement auditors must evaluate the five components of internal control: control environment, risk assessment, control activities, information and communication, and monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The understanding obtained from this assessment must be documented in the working papers to support the audit plan and subsequent testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working papers must document separate review of five components
rubrics_metrics.description: The audit program and working papers should include steps and documentation that separately review each of the five internal control components for each relevant compliance requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard audit programs that do not include separate steps for each component are deficient; reliance on Supplement guidance may partially offset planning deficiencies but auditors should still document component-level assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling plan documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Working papers must document the sampling plan including sampling objectives, population and its characteristics, sampling methodology, and criteria used to determine allowability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sampling objectives should be specific; identify whether costs tested are direct or indirect and whether they are for materials, overhead, or labor; identify the allowability criteria from OMB Circular A-122 being tested; documentation should allow determination of which procedures applied to each Federal award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of compliance testing (transactions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Working papers must document compliance requirement testing (examining transactions) sufficiently to support conclusions on compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation should include objectives, scope, methodology, sampling criteria, federal award number, name and type (grant/contract/cooperative agreement), voucher/documents reviewed (invoice, purchase order), and adequate description of tested transactions (cost type, amount, date/period, and whether charged directly or indirectly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Working papers must allow experienced auditor to determine supporting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Form and content of working papers should enable an experienced auditor to determine the evidence that supports significant conclusions and judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a GAGAS requirement; insufficient documentation (e.g., only a check number) is inadequate to determine adequacy of performed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-testing and acceptance where documentation inadequate
rubrics_metrics.description: If working papers are insufficient, re-testing by the reviewer may be used to obtain reasonable assurance of auditor conclusions, and may allow acceptance of audit conclusions despite documentation weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although re-testing can mitigate inadequate documentation, auditors should still correct deficiencies to meet standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination between audit organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Audits subject to Circular A-133 must be planned to build on work performed by others; auditee and auditors should coordinate single audit work to avoid duplication and to achieve efficient, cost-effective audits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination includes pre-audit meetings, engagement letters referencing coordination requirements, and documentation of what work can be relied upon between organizations (e.g., DCAA and independent public accountants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documented reliance on other auditors' work
rubrics_metrics.description: When relying on other audit organizations' work, auditors must identify pertinent work that can be relied upon and document the reliance and basis for doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliance is limited if the other organization's working papers are inadequately documented; auditors should identify reports (e.g., DCAA timekeeping audits) that could support audit conclusions and document the basis for reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Uniform Quality Control Guide for A-133 Audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality control reviews should be conducted using the approved Uniform Quality Control Guide for the A-133 Audits (1999 edition referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guide is the approved checklist for performing quality control review procedures under the President’s Council on Integrity and Efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to GAGAS and AICPA standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Audits must comply with Generally Accepted Government Auditing Standards (GAGAS) and generally accepted auditing standards issued by the AICPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality control reviews evaluate compliance with these standards in planning, testing, documentation, and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on internal control and compliance (content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditors must issue reports on internal control over compliance and on compliance with laws, regulations, and provisions of contracts or grant agreements, including an opinion on compliance of major programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reports are required elements of the A-133 reporting package and must reflect tested compliance requirements and internal control assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit program must include steps to document understanding of five internal control elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit engagement programs should be revised to include explicit audit steps that document an understanding of the five internal control elements related to each of the applicable compliance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to auditors (Arthur Andersen in the report) to revise standard audit programs to meet Circular A-133 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working papers should document judgments, procedures, and conclusions with sufficient evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Working papers must record auditors' judgments, the procedures performed, and the results or conclusions with relevant and sufficient evidence including the sampling plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to improve working papers so they adequately support auditor conclusions and permit reliance by other audit organizations and reviewers.
